The chronicity (4 months), mucus, and lack of systemic alarm features raise suspicion for either irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhea (IBS-D) or mild-moderate inflammatory bowel disease (e.g., quiescent or low-grade ulcerative colitis or microscopic colitis). Microscopic colitis (lymphocytic or collagenous) commonly presents with chronic watery diarrhea, normal weight, and mucus — and is often missed without specific testing. Celiac disease and bile acid malabsorption are also plausible. Next, I should assess stool consistency (to distinguish watery vs. loose vs. fatty), dietary triggers (e.g., lactose, gluten), and associated abdominal symptoms (pain, urgency, bloating) — all helpful in differentiating IBS-D, microscopic colitis, and celiac.
